text:
Anya Rivera: quick design review — proposing a compact view for Prompt Sets in Evals. Screenshot (annotated): https://img.redwood.internal/ux/compact-props.png. Main asks: legibility of score badges, keyboard nav, and copy for the approve flow. Thoughts?
Tom Chu: looks promising. score badges are kinda low contrast on dark bg — 2 of 3 fail AA.
Lia Patel: agree on contrast. target 4.5:1 for normal text. also font-weight feels too light in compact mode.
Shawn O'Neill: compact toggle makes sense for power users, but we should not shrink touch targets below 44px height.
Anya Rivera: good point re touch. also worried about accidental approve when compacted — maybe move primary action to right, add extra confirm step?
Jenna (design-bot): Accessibility checklist run: keyboard focus order, visible focus ring, aria-labels for toolbar icons, and contrast tokens. Marked 3 failures: badge contrast, focus outline too faint, missing aria-pressed for toggle.
Tom Chu: noted. keyboard nav currently skips collapsed rows; I can add tabindex and proper roving focus.
Lia Patel: copy suggestion: change button from `Approve suite` to `Approve & Run` — shorter and indicates action. but check translations.
Shawn O'Neill: +1 for `Approve & Run`. also proposing an inline diff icon next to each prompt so reviewers can peek changes without leaving the list.
Anya Rivera: inline diff preview is great. it should open a side panel, not a modal, so keyboard focus stays predictable.
Jenna (design-bot): suggested focus CSS for consistency: ```
:focus{outline:3px solid #1a73e8;outline-offset:2px}
``` Run this through contrast tool for the outline color.
Tom Chu: will implement focus style and run contrast. Lia, can you pick new badge colors? maybe try darker gray for low scores and a saturated accent for high.
Lia Patel: will iterate palette — will aim for 4.5:1 with background.
QA-bot: @Tom added E2E test case 'promptsets_compact_keyboard' in TestRail ID 4521 for keyboard traversal and focus.
Anya Rivera: cool. last nit — scorecards in compact mode lose the label hierarchy. can we keep small bold label above the number?
Shawn O'Neill: keep semantic hierarchy, yes. bold label + reduced number size works.
Tom Chu: I'll push a branch and drop a demo link here when ready.
Anya Rivera: thanks team. can we do a quick sync tomorrow 10:00am PT to finalize copy and a11y fixes? :calendar: 
Shawn O'Neill: 👍
Lia Patel: see you then.
Jenna (design-bot): Follow-ups created: #ux-contrast, #a11y-bugs, #dev-compact-mode.
